title: DXY vs. Broad USD Comparator
question: How does DXY differ conceptually from a broad dollar measure when live DXY values are not republished?
whyItMatters: DXY remains useful for basket-composition education, but Three Dials v2 uses the Federal Reserve broad dollar index as its public numeric dollar measure.
inputs: Federal Reserve broad-dollar evidence when a v2 snapshot is published
Real-rate and funding-pressure context from the same v2 snapshot
dataCadence: Three Dials v2 may supply dated Broad USD, real-yield and funding-pressure evidence. No live DXY observation is republished by this tool.
timestampRule: Show the snapshot week and each source observation date. Label the normal Monday/Tuesday publication window explicitly, and disable comparison if the latest published snapshot falls outside the approved cadence.
steps: Review how DXY basket composition can differ from a broad trade-weighted dollar measure.
Use the exercise conceptually; the live DXY comparison remains disabled unless a separate redistribution basis is approved.
agreement: DXY and broad USD moving in the same direction increase confidence that the move is wider than one currency pair.
Rates or stress moving consistently with the dollar direction strengthen the regime interpretation.
divergence: A strong DXY move with weak broad confirmation can be basket-led or foreign-currency-specific.
A quiet DXY with a firmer broad measure can understate pressure outside the legacy basket.
Mixed rates or stress should reduce confidence rather than be averaged away.
limitations: Three Dials v2 deliberately does not republish a live DXY value.
The comparator is conceptual and does not forecast any asset.
The page does not transmit or persist the reader's classifications.

title: Dollar Transmission Chain
question: Through which channel is the dollar reaching the asset now?
whyItMatters: The same dollar move can transmit through pricing, funding, opportunity cost, risk and hedge demand, or portfolio flows. The channel determines how the asset evidence should be read.
inputs: Liquidity, risk appetite and asset-specific evidence
dataCadence: Conceptual framework; pair it with the dated Daily or Weekly evidence linked on the page.
timestampRule: Use the publication timestamp of the linked evidence, not the framework page review date, as the market-data timestamp.
steps: Identify the upstream policy, rate or funding driver.
Check whether asset-specific evidence confirms or overrides that channel.
agreement: Aligned upstream and asset-specific evidence make the explanation more coherent.
Cross-asset confirmation can strengthen the channel diagnosis.
divergence: A physical supply shock can overpower the dollar channel in oil or gas.
Confidence demand can offset real-rate pressure in gold.
Asset-specific access or positioning can temporarily dominate in Bitcoin or FX.
limitations: A conceptual chain is not a causal proof for every daily move.
The framework does not supply entries, exits, position sizes or targets.
Asset-specific primary evidence remains required.

title: Three-Dial Macro Dashboard
question: What kind of dollar environment are the assets trading inside?
whyItMatters: Broad USD direction, real-rate pressure and funding pressure create the public weekly regime screen before asset-specific interpretation.
dataCadence: Qualitative weekly review, refreshed from the latest available dollar, real-yield and stress evidence.
timestampRule: Record the newest source timestamp for each dial and flag asynchronous inputs rather than presenting one false common timestamp.
steps: Record SOFR-minus-IORB funding pressure, then write one non-predictive regime sentence.
agreement: Aligned dials support a clearer rate-led, stress-led or easier-dollar description.
Cross-asset behavior can confirm the description after it is written.
divergence: Mixed dials indicate a transitional or asset-specific environment.
DXY, credit, volatility and broader liquidity evidence remain contextual confirmation rather than public v2 dial inputs.
limitations: Version 2 is a methodology break from the prior DXY/credit/volatility implementation.
The dashboard organizes observable conditions; it does not predict returns.
SOFR minus IORB is a funding-pressure indicator, not a complete liquidity/stress measure.
It is qualitative and must not be presented as the Weekly Score formula.

title: Weekly USD Impact Score
question: Is the cross-asset system behaving more like stronger-dollar pressure, weaker-dollar or liquidity support, or a mixed transition?
whyItMatters: The score compresses a fixed cross-asset input set into an auditable weekly regime reading that can be compared with the qualitative framework.
inputs: Published score inputs and signed weights
Timestamp, version and archived publication vintage
dataCadence: Weekly after the input window closes and the production pipeline publishes the score.
timestampRule: Verify the dashboard timestamp, methodology version, active input set and archived publication vintage before comparison.
steps: Check the score timestamp, version and active input set.
Read the zone and components rather than treating the decimal as a precise forecast.
Compare with the three-dial reading and investigate local shocks or contradictions.
agreement: Agreement with the qualitative dials increases coherence, not certainty.
A stable archived vintage makes the comparison auditable.
divergence: Supply shocks, policy pivots and asset-specific flows are expected weak zones.
A score and a qualitative reading can differ because they answer related but non-identical questions.
limitations: The score is not a model portfolio, forecast, trading system or recommendation.
Historical regime alignment is not an asset-return statistic.
The score must not be used alone for suitability, entries, exits or position sizing.

title: Weekly Regime Lab
question: Can the reader form a disciplined weekly regime read from dated evidence before seeing the deterministic classifications and separate Score output?
whyItMatters: Recording the three dials, dominant-driver hypothesis and conditional explanation before comparison reduces anchoring and turns Chapter 11 into a repeatable practice routine.
inputs: Dated SOFR-minus-IORB funding-pressure observation, plus a browser-local driver hypothesis and conditional written reading
dataCadence: Latest repository-published completed-week Three-Dials snapshot with an exact-week Score bridge. No market data is retrieved in the browser.
timestampRule: Show the snapshot week and every source observation date. Keep the normal Monday/Tuesday publication window explicit, and disable deterministic comparison if the snapshot is outside the approved cadence.
steps: Read the dated facts and record the three dials plus an unscored dominant-driver hypothesis.
Write what supports the reading and what would challenge it before seeing any deterministic labels.
Submit the browser-local reading, compare only the three deterministic dials, then inspect the separate exact-week Score output and return to the relevant chapter or Weekly report.
agreement: Use aligned, partly aligned or materially different for the three deterministic dials rather than correct or incorrect.
Agreement shows process coherence, not predictive accuracy; the dominant-driver hypothesis remains unscored.
divergence: A broad-dollar disagreement points back to the dollar-measure discussion in Chapter 3.
A real-rate or funding-pressure disagreement points back to Chapter 11 and the relevant primary evidence.
A driver disagreement is not machine-scored; compare the hypothesis qualitatively with the Weekly report and transmission framework.
limitations: The evidence is a dated completed-week repository snapshot, not real-time market data.
No classification, confidence selection, driver hypothesis or written response is stored or transmitted.
Only the three deterministic dials are compared; the driver hypothesis is deliberately unscored.
The exact-week USD Impact Score v2 is revealed separately and is not an answer key, forecast or trading signal.

title: Weekly Dollar Regime Checklist
question: What is the minimum ordered evidence set needed for a repeatable weekly review?
whyItMatters: A compact checklist protects the reading order from headline noise and makes unresolved contradictions visible.
inputs: Asset-specific physical, flow, volatility and positioning evidence
dataCadence: Weekly operating routine using the latest completed releases for each input.
timestampRule: Record source-specific timestamps and identify any input that has not refreshed since its expected release.
steps: Add the relevant asset-specific primary evidence.
Record the regime sentence, contradictions and next verification point.
agreement: A completed ordered checklist makes the evidence trail reviewable.
Repeated use improves consistency even when the result remains mixed.
divergence: Do not delete contradictions to make the narrative cleaner.
Return to the relevant chapter when the sequence or channel is unclear.
limitations: A checklist cannot replace primary-source verification.
Completion does not imply that a regime interpretation will predict returns.
The checklist is educational and non-personalized.
